content.user_title: Build Persistent Azure AI Agents in Java
content.value_statement: Java developers need reliable patterns for Azure AI Agents workflows. This skill explains SDK setup, authentication, agents, threads, messages, runs, responses, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for com.azure:azure-ai-agents-persistent.
Outlines the agent, thread, message, run, polling, response, and cleanup workflow.
Compares synchronous and asynchronous client roles.
Shows basic HttpResponseException handling for SDK calls.
limitations: Uses a beta SDK version, so APIs may change.
Does not provision Azure resources or model deployments.
Does not include a complete runnable application.
Does not deeply cover tool calls, RequiresAction handling, or streaming details.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Java Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Create a small service flow that creates an agent, sends a message, runs it, and reads the response.

use_cases.title: Plan Azure SDK Integration
use_cases.description: Review the required client, authentication, endpoint, and lifecycle concepts before adding Azure AI Agents to a system.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Resource Hygiene
use_cases.description: Use the cleanup and polling guidance to reduce abandoned threads, agents, and incomplete run handling.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add the Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK to a Java project and list the required environment values.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the steps to create an agent, create a thread, add a user message, run the agent, and read messages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Run Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to poll an Azure AI Agents run, handle terminal statuses, and clean up resources after completion.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Java Azure AI Agents integration for authentication, lifecycle cleanup, run status handling, and error handling gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a setup checklist for a new Java service.
output_examples.output: The response lists the Maven package, endpoint value, model deployment name, Azure credential setup, and first client creation step.

output_examples.input: I need to understand the full agent lifecycle.
output_examples.output: The response explains creating an agent, creating a thread, adding a message, running the agent, polling status, listing messages, and deleting resources.

output_examples.input: I need to harden my sample before sharing it with my team.
output_examples.output: The response calls out missing run status checks, missing cleanup, weak error handling, and places where configuration should stay outside source control.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity or approved developer credentials.
Delete temporary threads and agents after tests to control cost and clutter.
Handle every run status, including failed, cancelled, and requires action.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode endpoints, credentials, or model deployment names in source control.
Do not poll too aggressively or ignore service rate limits.
Do not leave sample agents and threads running after experiments.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you use the Azure AI Agents Persistent SDK for Java to create and manage agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains SDK usage after your Azure project, endpoint, and model deployment already exist.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows the DefaultAzureCredential pattern and keeps credential setup outside the skill content.

faq.question: Can I use asynchronous clients?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill identifies the synchronous and asynchronous client roles, but examples focus on the synchronous client.

faq.question: Is the referenced package version final?
faq.answer: The skill references version 1.0.0-beta.1, so verify the current package version before production use.

faq.question: Does it include cleanup guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes deleting threads and agents after use to reduce cost and resource clutter.
